assets.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE finished square Steam Workshop cover for the original mod PHOBOS AUTO NAV for Ostranauts. Output a genuinely detailed 2048 x 2048 master, square composition. Original illustration, not a screenshot or official game asset.
Art direction: closely match the utilitarian overhead pixel-art world of Blue Bottle Games' Ostranauts: grounded hard science-fiction, a cramped working ship, angular patchwork floor plates, cream cabinets, slate-grey control casings, muted navy and teal, restrained mustard hazard accents, black recesses. Clearly visible purposeful pixel clusters, stepped edges, limited tonal bands, crisp nearest-neighbour appearance. No smooth 3D render, no painterly brushwork, no anime, no glossy space fantasy, no lens flares. Strong readable silhouettes and calm editorial composition, not dense micro-detail.
Series cover layout: charcoal metal surround with thin muted ochre rules and four unobtrusive corner fasteners. Upper quarter is a dark flat nameplate. At top-left render the exact small word "PHOBOS" in widely spaced warm ivory industrial capitals. Immediately below it, very large bold condensed warm ivory capitals read "AUTO NAV", across almost full width, impeccably legible at thumbnail size. Small muted teal accent square beside PHOBOS. Beneath the big title a single modest uppercase line reads exactly "APPROACH / BRAKE / DOCK". Bottom narrow dark footer, exact readable small text "FOR OSTRANAUTS". Leave 5% safe margins around all lettering.
Main scene, below title: overhead cutaway of a practical little salvage ship's navigation compartment. A dark U-shaped console with an empty central pilot chair, cream avionics cabinets, chunky physical knobs, simple teal CRT navigation traces. Centre this distinctive nav console large in lower-left foreground. Through the composition's open space on upper-right, a smaller overhead asymmetric working spacecraft approaches a simple industrial docking port with a clear safe gap. Show a restrained dotted teal approach path and a small braking marker, subtle navigation illustration rather than magical projected UI. Short tiny white RCS puffs only. Everything belongs to the same overhead projection; no perspective horizon. Dense black empty space beyond the hull gives scale. Convey measured manoeuvres, maintained equipment and survival through careful navigation. The console dominates, ships subordinate. No weapon fire, no racing speed streaks, no giant torch exhaust, no large radar dish. No other readable text, fake stats, real company logos, official Ostranauts logo, NASA marks, or endorsement badges. Render only the requested exact text.

Grounded hard science-fiction, cramped working ship, angular patchwork floor plates, cream cabinets, slate-grey casings, muted navy and teal, restrained mustard hazard accents, black recesses. Purposeful visible pixel clusters, stepped edges and limited tonal bands with a crisp nearest-neighbour appearance. Large readable silhouettes; no smooth 3D render, painterly brushwork, anime, glossy space fantasy, lens flares or dense decorative micro-detail.
This belongs to a coordinated cover series. Exact shared layout: square charcoal metal surround, thin muted ochre rules, one unobtrusive fastener in each corner. Upper 29% is a dark flat nameplate. At top-left a small muted teal square followed by widely letter-spaced warm ivory industrial pixel capitals "PHOBOS". Beneath that, the mod title occupies a very large single line nearly the whole nameplate width, bold condensed warm ivory industrial capitals. Beneath a thin ochre rule is the modest uppercase subline. Lower scene fills the remaining interior down to a narrow dark footer. Bottom footer exact small readable text "FOR OSTRANAUTS". Minimum 5% safe margins for all typography. Typography must stay readable when reduced to 256px. Render only the requested exact text, with no other labels, fake stats, official game logo, real company logo, NASA/ESA marks or endorsement badges.
Title text exactly "FRAMEWORK". Subline exactly "SHARED SYSTEMS".
Scene: an original diagrammatic overhead cutaway of a compact utilitarian spacecraft's service backbone, combining physical industrial imagery with a quiet schematic to communicate a SHARED SOFTWARE LIBRARY. At centre is a prominent rectangular dark modular backplane with three cream-and-slate removable cartridges neatly seated in parallel slots and one visibly empty service slot, chunky copper contacts and service fasteners. Thin restrained teal schematic lines branch from this central assembly to THREE much smaller contextual shipboard scenes around it: a CRT navigation station, a clamped wall-panel recovery fixture, and a tiny contained green crop cassette. These vignettes are subtly ghosted technical insets, clearly a conceptual relationship, not literal pipes that grant free power or food. Place the main backplane at centre lower half, dominate the composition with its clear silhouette and ordered connections. Patchwork steel deck and simple overhead cutaway hull edges enclose the composition; black void visible outside the hull. Evoke maintainable shared infrastructure that lets specialised systems work together. No humans, robots, giant new reactor, puzzle-piece clipart, fantasy energy core, infinity symbols or promise of self-sustaining life support. The physical backplane is a visual metaphor for software, not a new player-obtainable machine. Keep crop inset very small. Balanced disciplined arrangement with quiet breathing room.

Scene: an original overhead cutaway of an onboard salvage-processing bay, a practical shipboard workshop rather than an exterior space battle. Main foreground hero on the left is a square 4x4 dismantling fixture: a charcoal rectangular work bed, blue side rails with small mustard holding clamps, a pale cream service box and a blue control box at the rear, a single cross-member gripping one ALREADY DETACHED rectangular grey hull panel. Distinct coarse pixel clusters and silhouette make the fixture recognisable. To its right and slightly higher stands a larger electric furnace: square pale grey chassis, dominant circular CLOSED dark crucible lid with concentric rings, cream electrical box at left, blue coolant housings at right and a short ochre access step in front. It is electrical, without torch beams or a glowing fusion core. A small confined amber process-light accent is enough. Modest separate radiator fins and a sealed receiver are suggested at the back. In the foreground a small orderly pile of recovered steel and aluminium stock, together with a clearly separate dark residue container: material recovery has remainders. Floor plates, service access and limited separately installed conduits. The salvage equipment occupies roughly 70% of the scene; no humans needed. No cutting an attached hull, no explosion, no endless conveyor factory, no external laser, no nuclear emblem, no flying sparks filling the cabin. Render an honest promotional illustration of finite onboard recovery and maintenance.

Scene: an original overhead cutaway of a small habitable spacecraft cultivation bay. Two practical rectangular cream-and-slate cultivation racks occupy the centre, containing modest rows of green leafy crops in SEALED ROOT CASSETTES. One holds small potato plants, the other recognisable lettuce rosettes. These are compact serviceable machines, not lush wilderness or a glass dome. Thin lamp bars, modest ventilation grilles, finite small water reservoirs, capped tubing and replaceable nutrient cartridges communicate the work and consumables behind growth. Leaves use broad readable pixel clusters in muted natural greens against cream and charcoal housings. One small tray of several harvested potatoes and two lettuce heads sits by an accessible aisle, with restrained tending tools. A tiny empty stool or galley corner supplies a human habitation cue without any character. Warm ivory grow-light accent, practical metal deck under the racks, small black void visible outside a cutaway hull corner. Calm, resource-conscious and hopeful within a harsh industrial world. No wheat, fruit trees, flowers, giant jungle, unlimited water, open flooding troughs, outdoor soil field, panoramic greenhouse or claim to feed a whole crew indefinitely. This illustrates authored gameplay equipment and crops, not a scientific demonstration. Keep the machine silhouettes and foliage large enough to recognise at thumbnail size.

dimensionNote: The tool returned 1254 x 1254 images despite the 2048 request. Retained unchanged, not upscaled; all exceed 2x the 512px export.
